title: Opportunistic Merge-Pause Scheduler with Predictive KV Footprint Throttling
creator: Aisha Natarajan
description:
Problem: Continuous-batching improves throughput but interacts poorly with KV cache residency and GPU memory fragmentation when high-priority low-latency tenants arrive. Existing preemption strategies either (a) aggressively evict KV entries causing quality regressions and repeated cold-starts, or (b) stall throughput by full batch drains, increasing cost and p99 latency for background work.

Proposal summary: Implement an "opportunistic merge-pause" scheduler that, on high-priority arrival, (1) pauses low-priority inflight slices instead of full eviction, (2) opportunistically merges small pending requests into transient micro-batches to preserve GPU utilization, and (3) uses a predictive KV footprint estimator to decide whether to evict, snapshot, or hold KV pages based on predicted reuse and model working-set impact. The goal is SLO-aware preemption that balances tail latency for high-priority requests with throughput and KV hit-rate for background tenants.

Key features: 
- Pause semantics: mark slices as paused with soft-reservation tokens allowing quick resume without full KV eviction.
- Opportunistic merge: combine small paused slices from multiple low-priority tenants into short-lived batches to amortize kernel launch cost while avoiding KV churn.
- Predictive KV throttling: lightweight estimator (histogram + LRU age + tenant hotness predictor) that outputs a decision: keep-in-place, snapshot-to-host, or evict.
- Memory-aware decisions: take into account GPU fragmentation and estimated compaction cost; trigger a compact-and-merge operation only when net latency benefit is positive.

Success metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency for high-priority tenants, throughput (tokens/sec) for background tiers, KV hit-rate after preemption events, number of eviction-induced cold-starts, GPU memory fragmentation metric, and cost-per-token.

Rollout plan: spike -> internal canary on dedicated pool -> runtime release (runtime-1.22) with opt-in flag -> gradual enable by tenant tier with telemetry gates.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha N: Wrote initial design sketch and shared in #runtime-architecture. Linked design doc: https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/RUNTIME/merge-pause-scheduler

2026-03-04 - Marco: Completed spike to measure resume overhead (kernel rebind + KV pointer fixups). Observed median resume time 6ms for small slices (<= 32 tokens), p95 ~28ms. Patch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4421

2026-03-06 - Eng team review: Discussed fairness risk where low-volume background tenants could be starved by repeated merges. Decided to add a per-tenant merge-budget expressed as micro-batch credits refreshed per-second. Action: implement budget and meter in scheduler core.

2026-03-07 - Marco: Added predictive KV estimator prototype. Uses a tiny decaying count sketch + recency window to predict reuse probability. Simulation on production traces (7 days) shows 18% fewer evictions vs LRU under identical memory pressure, KV hit-rate +6% for background tier.

2026-03-09 - QA: Found a regression in GPU memory fragmentation after long runs with many merges; root cause: temporary buffers not freed promptly by upstream allocator. Created follow-up ENG-220002 to address allocator callback semantics.
2026-03-10 - PM (Rosa Chen): Confirmed customer impact trade-offs acceptable for beta customers; prioritized canary with two dedicated pools (beta-high, beta-low).

2026-03-11 - Marco: Benchmarked canary scenario against baseline preempt-to-evict policy. Results: high-priority p99 reduced by 35% relative to baseline, background throughput dropped 7% but KV cold-starts reduced 43%. Preparing runtime-1.22 feature flag PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4478

2026-03-12 - Security review note: no new network flows; but needing a quick audit of snapshot-to-host behavior for tenant isolation. Assigned to security team: security-review required=false for prototype, but full release will require review.
